title: Request-contract-aware shedder and graceful autoscaler handoff for SLO-preserving multi-region failover
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design and implement a request-contract-aware load shedder that coordinates with readiness transitions and the autoscaler to preserve customer-facing SLOs during multi-region failovers and capacity pressure. This ticket covers: (1) defining lightweight request contracts and priorities, (2) a local shedder that applies budgeted shedding per-worker and respects prefix/KV cache hotness, (3) a graceful handoff path that pauses readiness transitions while autoscaler drains/ramps, and (4) circuit-breaker integration to avoid cascading autoscale spikes. The goal is predictable SLO preservation (p99 latency and error budget policies) even when traffic surges or regions fail over.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Maya T.: Kickoff notes: Spike showed that naive shedding at the L7 edge caused significant tail-latency regressions due to cold KV-cache misses. We need local-first shedding that understands cache hotness and request criticality.

2026-02-22 - Olu: Prototype implemented: a lightweight in-process shedder that classifies requests by contract (interactive|async|control) and applies probabilistic shedding weighted by contract priority. Early results: 18% overall request reduction under overload with <2% p99 latency increase for interactive requests.

2026-02-24 - Design review (K. Lin): Recommend exposing contract tags in SDKs and platform ingress to make classification robust; also add a fallback policy for unknown contracts (default to low priority).

2026-02-26 - PM feedback (R. Alvarez): Must ensure shedder decisions are included in billing logs and observability metrics for post-incident RCA and customer communication. Add token-level shed counters to console.

2026-02-28 - Eng: Implemented graceful readiness hold: when autoscaler receives a drain signal we mark node readiness as 'draining-wait' which prevents immediate readiness flip and allows KV-cache warming in target region during failover. Unit tests added for readiness state transitions.

2026-03-01 - Security (J. Park): Reviewed contract metadata surface area. Confirmed no sensitive data flows; recommended adding HMAC on contract headers to prevent tampering by intermediate proxies. Added security_review_required flag.

2026-03-02 - Perf: Load test #3 (multi-region failover simulation): Enabled shedder + readiness-hold + autoscaler hysteresis. Result: During simulated us-east outage, controlled shed preserved interactive p99 under SLO while noncritical async queue latency degraded gracefully. Autoscaler did not overshoot target capacity in eu-west. Dashboard link in attachments.

2026-03-03 - Next steps: Codify rollout plan (canary region), add Console metrics dashboards for per-contract shedding rates, and prepare runbook for operator-driven failovers. Open PR for review: runtime PR #2284.
